citations.quote: The tax credit shall be equal to 10% of the Federal earned income tax credit received by the taxpayer for the same taxable year.
citations.source: Act of Nov. 12, 2025, P.L. 156, No. 45 (The Fiscal Code, Art. XVI-W.2, Working Pennsylvanians Tax Credit)

citations.quote: If the amount of credit which the qualified taxpayer is eligible to receive under this section exceeds the qualified taxpayer's tax liability, the department shall refund the excess amount to the qualified taxpayer.
citations.source: Act of Nov. 12, 2025, P.L. 156, No. 45 (The Fiscal Code, Art. XVI-W.2)

citations.quote: This article shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024.
citations.source: Act of Nov. 12, 2025, P.L. 156, No. 45 (The Fiscal Code, Art. XVI-W.2)

citations.quote: This is a refundable tax credit, meaning you can receive it even if you don't owe Pennsylvania income tax.
citations.source: Pennsylvania Department of Revenue, Working Pennsylvanians Tax Credit

summary: Act 45 of 2025 created Pennsylvania's Working Pennsylvanians Tax Credit, codified at Fiscal Code Art. XVI-W.2. The credit equals 10% of the federal EITC, is refundable, and applies to taxable years beginning after 12/31/2024, which includes 2026. This head of household has 3 qualifying children, $60,000 of earned income and $60,010 of AGI. Under the Rev. Proc. 2025-32 parameters (maximum credit $8,231, phase-out from $23,890 at 21.06%), the federal EITC is $624.13, so the WPTC is $62.41. The engine's steps match the law, and the consensus answer of $0 overlooks the new credit. The only possible difference is a few cents if the federal EITC is rounded to the IRS $50-bracket table (about $62.10).
